ja: 最近、週末は何をしてるの？
en: What do you do on weekends these days?
alternatives: What are you doing on weekends these days?
These days, what do you do on weekends?
point: 習慣は現在形 do。「最近」は these days

ja: 仕事は相変わらず忙しいけど、最近は週末に料理教室に通ってるんだ。
en: Even though work is still busy, I've been taking a cooking class on weekends lately.
alternatives: Although work is as busy as ever, I've been going to a cooking class on weekends recently.
Work's still busy, but lately I've been taking cooking classes on weekends.
point: 続いている習慣は現在完了進行形 I've been taking

ja: もしあの時あの会社を辞めてなかったら、僕は今の妻には出会ってなかっただろうね。
en: If I hadn't quit that company back then, I never would have met my wife.
alternatives: If I hadn't quit that job back then, I probably wouldn't have met my wife.
If I hadn't left that company back then, I wouldn't have met my wife.
point: 過去の仮定は if + had 過去分詞、帰結は would have 過去分詞

ja: うちの兄、大学のときにもっと真剣に英語を勉強しておけばよかったって、最近よく言ってるんだ。
en: These days my brother keeps saying he wishes he'd studied English more seriously in college.
alternatives: Lately my brother keeps saying he wishes he had studied English harder in college.
These days my brother often says he wishes he'd taken English more seriously in college.
point: 過去を悔やむ wish の後は had + 過去分詞

ja: 駅前の本屋で働いてたタカシ、今はカナダに住んでるらしいよ。
en: Takashi, who used to work at the bookstore by the station, is apparently living in Canada now.
alternatives: I heard Takashi, who used to work at the bookstore by the station, lives in Canada now.
Apparently Takashi, the guy who used to work at the bookstore near the station, is living in Canada now.
point: 「働いてた」は used to work、人の説明は who でつなぐ

ja: 妹は今留学中で、ホストファミリーからたくさん役立つアドバイスをもらってるらしいよ。
en: My sister is studying abroad, and apparently she's getting a lot of useful advice from her host family.
alternatives: My sister's studying abroad now, and I hear she's getting lots of helpful advice from her host family.
My sister is studying abroad, and it sounds like her host family is giving her a lot of useful advice.
point: advice は数えられないので advices にしない

ja: 引っ越してから一番大変だったのは、仕事じゃなくて、近所に知り合いが一人もいないことだったよ。
en: What was hardest after I moved wasn't the job but the fact that I didn't know a single person in the neighborhood.
alternatives: The hardest thing after I moved wasn't the job; it was not knowing anyone in the neighborhood.
What was hardest after the move wasn't work but not knowing a single person nearby.
point: What was hardest で主語を作り、wasn't A but B でつなぐ

ja: 君が前に住んでたアパートの隣のラーメン屋って、まだやってる？
en: Is the ramen shop next to your old apartment still in business?
alternatives: Is that ramen place next to the apartment you used to live in still open?
Is the ramen shop next to where you used to live still around?
point: 「〜の隣の」は名詞の後ろに next to を置く

ja: 引っ越したこと、もっと早く君に知らせるべきだったよね。バタバタしてて忘れてたんだ。
en: I should have let you know sooner that I'd moved, but things got hectic and I forgot.
alternatives: I should have told you earlier that I'd moved, but I got busy and forgot.
I really should have told you about my move sooner, but things got hectic and it slipped my mind.
point: 「すべきだったのに」は should have + 過去分詞

ja: 妻と僕は去年、子どもたちとキャンプを始めたんだけど、すっかりハマっちゃってさ。
en: My wife and I took up camping with the kids last year, and we've really gotten into it.
alternatives: My wife and I started camping with the kids last year, and we've gotten really hooked on it.
Last year my wife and I took up camping with our kids, and now we're totally into it.
point: 「ハマっている」は今の状態なので現在完了か現在形で

ja: 最近転職したって聞いたんだけど、新しい職場はどうなのかなと思って。
en: I heard you recently changed jobs, and I was wondering how you're finding the new place.
alternatives: I heard you changed jobs recently, so I was wondering how you're getting on at the new place.
I heard you recently switched jobs, and I was wondering how things are going at your new workplace.
point: 「〜かなと思って」は I was wondering + 疑問詞で柔らかく

ja: 兄に、来週末の引っ越しを手伝ってって頼まれたんだ。
en: My brother asked me to help him move next weekend.
alternatives: My brother asked me to help with his move next weekend.
My brother asked if I could help him move next weekend.
point: ask + 人 + to do の形。me を忘れずに

ja: 彼女、最近は週末にギターを習うのにはまってるらしいよ。
en: I heard she's really into learning the guitar on weekends these days.
alternatives: Apparently she's gotten really into learning guitar on weekends lately.
I heard she's hooked on learning the guitar on weekends these days.
point: 前置詞 into の後ろは動名詞 learning

ja: 君が仕事を辞めて農業を始めたって聞いたときに驚いたのは、決断の早さだったよ。
en: What surprised me when I heard you'd quit your job to start farming was how quickly you made the decision.
alternatives: When I heard you'd quit your job to start farming, I was surprised by how quickly you decided.
When I heard you'd quit your job to become a farmer, what surprised me was how fast you made the decision.
point: 「驚いたのは〜だった」は What surprised me was で組み立てる

ja: 今の職場がもっと家から近かったら、平日でも君ともっと会えるのにな。
en: If my office were closer to home, I'd be able to see you more often during the week.
alternatives: If my office was closer to home, I could see you more often on weekdays.
If I worked closer to home, I'd get to see you more often during the week.
point: 現実と違う仮定は if 節を過去形、主節は would/could

ja: あのとき転職してなかったら、僕は今ごろまだ毎晩終電で帰ってたと思う。
en: If I hadn't changed jobs back then, I'd probably still be taking the last train home every night.
alternatives: If I hadn't switched jobs back then, I'd probably still be catching the last train home every night.
I think I'd still be taking the last train home every night if I hadn't changed jobs back then.
point: 過去の仮定は had done、今の結果は would be

ja: 転職したんだけど、今の会社のほうが前の会社よりずっと働きやすいよ。
en: I changed jobs, and my new company is much easier to work for than my old one.
alternatives: I switched jobs, and my current company is a lot easier to work for than my last one.
I changed jobs, and working at my new company is much easier than at my old one.
point: 比較級の強調は very ではなく much / a lot

ja: 兄は今、カナダで英語を勉強しているよ。
en: My brother is studying English in Canada now.
alternatives: My brother is now studying English in Canada.
My brother is in Canada studying English now.
point: 今していることは is と動詞の ing 形で言う

ja: ケンがまだあの会社で働いてるかどうか、知ってる？最近全然連絡取ってなくて。
en: Do you know whether Ken is still working at that company? I haven't been in touch with him lately.
alternatives: Do you happen to know if Ken still works at that company? I haven't talked to him in a while.
Do you know if Ken's still at that company? I haven't been in contact with him lately.
point: 「〜かどうか知ってる？」は Do you know if/whether + 平叙文の語順

ja: 最近、6 時に起きなきゃいけないんだ。
en: These days I have to get up at six.
alternatives: I have to wake up at six these days.
Recently I've had to get up at six.
point: 義務は have to + 動詞の原形

ja: 前に会ったとき、まだ部屋を探してたよね。もう引っ越したの？
en: You were still looking for an apartment when we last met. Have you moved yet?
alternatives: When we last met, you were still looking for an apartment. Have you moved yet?
You were still apartment hunting last time I saw you. Have you moved already?
point: 前回は過去進行形、今の状況は現在完了で聞く

ja: 赤ちゃんの写真、見せてもらえますか？
en: Could you show me photos of your baby?
alternatives: Can you show me photos of your baby?
Could you show me pictures of your baby?
point: 丁寧な依頼は Could you + 動詞の原形

ja: 来月こっちに戻ってきたら、久しぶりにみんなで集まらない？
en: When you come back here next month, why don't we get everyone together again?
alternatives: Once you're back here next month, how about we all get together again?
When you get back next month, should we get the whole group together again?
point: 来月のことでも when 節は現在形で言う

ja: この前ケンにばったり会ったら、来月から大阪に転勤になるって言ってたよ。
en: When I ran into Ken the other day, he told me he was being transferred to Osaka next month.
alternatives: I ran into Ken the other day, and he said he was being transferred to Osaka next month.
When I bumped into Ken the other day, he said he'd be transferred to Osaka next month.
point: 言ってた内容は時制を過去にずらし was being transferred に

ja: 姉はこの夏ずっとヨーロッパを旅して回ってて、節約のためにユースホステルに泊まってたよ。
en: My sister spent the whole summer traveling around Europe, staying in hostels to save money.
alternatives: My sister traveled around Europe all summer, staying in hostels to save money.
My sister spent all summer traveling around Europe, staying at hostels to save money.
point: 「泊まってた」は , staying と分詞で後ろにつなげる

ja: うちの父、最近お医者さんに毎朝30分歩かされてるんだよ。
en: My dad's doctor has been making him walk for thirty minutes every morning lately.
alternatives: Lately, my dad's doctor has been making him walk thirty minutes every morning.
My father's doctor has been making him go for a thirty-minute walk every morning lately.
point: make + 人 + 動詞の原形。to は付けない

ja: 最近、仕事がずっと忙しくて、趣味に使える時間がほとんどないんだ。
en: Work has been really busy lately, so I have hardly any time for my hobbies.
alternatives: I've been really busy with work lately, so I barely have any time for my hobbies.
Things have been hectic at work recently, so I hardly have any time for hobbies.
point: 「ほとんど〜ない」は hardly any で、not や no を重ねない

ja: 妹は去年結婚しただけじゃなくて、自分のお店まで開いたんだよ。
en: Not only did my sister get married last year, but she also opened her own shop.
alternatives: My sister not only got married last year but also opened her own shop.
My sister got married last year, and on top of that, she opened her own shop.
point: Not only を文頭に置くと did + 主語 + 原形の語順になる
